query: Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys reported to date commonly contain both solid solutions and intermetallic compounds. Induction-melted Al- and Mg-rich alloys reached densities of 2.64–2.75 g/cm3 but all had complex structures; Al20Be20Fe10Si15Ti35 combined a density of 3.91 g/cm3 with 911 HV hardness and oxidation resistance at 700 and 900 °C; compositionally graded MgAlCuZnGd showed region-dependent compression, plasticity, and corrosion behavior; and reported AlMgₓTiSnZn alloys contained a primary BCC constituent together with intermetallic compounds, with x = 1.0 showing the best property combination in that series. Prior studies have emphasized hardness and room-temperature compression, whereas interfacial segregation, interfacial energy, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance remain insufficiently studied. The design must retain a density below 6 g/cm3 and address performance constraints associated with the tendency of Mg and dissimilar constituent elements to form stable intermetallic compounds. Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state, what single intervention hypothesis could improve its combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance? State the intervention, its proposed causal mechanism, quantitative or directional predictions relative to the as-processed baseline, the composition and operating or test boundaries, the prior experimental evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a controlled experiment with explicit observations that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled amount of refractory elements into the Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy can improve its combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance by enhancing the formation of a stable, protective oxide layer and refining the microstructure.
generation.intervention: Addition of refractory elements (e.g., Hf, Mo, Nb, Ta, W) to the alloy composition
generation.conditions: High-temperature oxidation resistance, corrosion resistance, and mechanical properties (e.g., hardness, compression, plasticity) at temperatures up to 900 °C
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable, protective oxide layer and refinement of the microstructure
generation.mechanism: The refractory elements can enhance the formation of a stable, protective oxide layer, reducing oxidation and corrosion, while also refining the microstructure, leading to improved mechanical properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved high-temperature oxidation resistance, corrosion resistance, and mechanical properties (e.g., increased hardness, compression, and plasticity) compared to the as-processed baseline
generation.baseline: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state
generation.boundary: Density below 6 g/cm3, operating temperatures up to 900 °C
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount and type of refractory elements to add, as well as the potential effects on other material properties (e.g., ductility, fracture toughness)

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment with varying amounts of refractory elements added to the alloy composition, tested at high temperatures (up to 900 °C) for oxidation resistance, corrosion resistance, and mechanical properties
measurements: Oxidation resistance (e.g., weight gain, oxide layer thickness)
Corrosion resistance (e.g., corrosion rate, pit depth)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of refractory elements does not improve the high-temperature oxidation resistance, corrosion resistance, and mechanical properties of the alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

Gap and lever. Type: tradeoff. Statement: While hardness remains stable between 300 K and 600 K, the elastic modulus increases significantly due to a reduction in dislocation density, but this trend reverses at higher temperatures.. System: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating. Lever: temperature. Quote: "At 300 K and 600 K, the ordered lattice structure of the high entropy alloy coating material is basically the same, and thus its hardness is basically the same."

Gap and lever. Type: tradeoff. Statement: There is a trade-off between the high strength provided by the B2 matrix and the poor oxidation resistance caused by the formation of complex, unprotective oxides like TiNb2O7 and Nb2Zr6O17.. System: AlNbTiVZr 0.25. Lever: phase composition (B2 matrix vs. complex oxides). Quote: "The high strength of the alloy at ambient and elevated temperatures was attributed to a strong solid solution strengthening induced by Zr and the B2 ordered matrix phase."

Gap and lever. Type: limitation. Statement: The study only examined oxidation at two specific temperatures (1000 °C and 1300 °C), leaving the behavior at intermediate or other temperatures unexplored.. System: MoNbTaTiW RHEA with Si-20Cr-20Fe coating. Lever: oxidation temperature. Quote: "To show the anti-oxidation mechanism of the silicide coating, the evolution of the structure and compositions of the coating at 1000 °C and 1300 °C were studied."

Gap and lever. Type: open_problem. Statement: The softening resistance of the designed alloys above 700 °C is not yet optimized and requires further alloy design strategies to improve.. System: L2 1 precipitation-strengthened lightweight high-entropy alloys. Lever: addition of minor refractory elements. Quote: "As the temperature increases to 700 °C, the yield strengths of Alloys 1 and 8 are still kept at 607 ± 22 MPa and 643 ± 16 MPa, respectively, though an obvious softening occurs like many other precipitation-strengthened ferritic BCC alloys."
